text:
The clearest matched-negative comparison is Petrov and Macdonald’s [gSASRec (2023), §6.2.4](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.07192): SASRec/BERT4Rec trained with BCE, generalized BCE, or sampled softmax using uniform negatives, K∈{1,4,16,64,256}. No universal softmax advantage: SASRec Recall@1 at K=16 was 0.0673 BCE versus 0.0635 softmax; gBCE reached 0.0769. At K=256, NDCG@10 was similar across objectives. These are full-catalog evaluation findings. [Turning Dross Into Gold Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602) supports improving SASRec through softmax training, but its headline full-softmax versus original one-negative BCE comparison does not isolate loss from negative count. Huang’s [Revisiting Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation (2025)](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.09596v1) proposes investigations of padding, positional embeddings and sampling; it reports no matched-negative BCE/softmax experiment.

Controls matter: gSASRec defines BCE as the sum over one positive plus K negatives divided by K+1. Averaging positive and negative losses separately changes their relative weighting as K grows; report this explicitly. Match sampled items, collision/history exclusions, valid-position averaging, optimizer tuning and compute. [Wu et al., On the Effectiveness of Sampled Softmax](https://arxiv.org/html/2201.02327) analyzes cosine normalization, temperature and representation magnitudes in collaborative filtering—not a controlled SASRec comparison. Consequently, treating embedding normalization/temperature as separate ablations is warranted. Unobserved items can be false negatives; matching exclusion rules controls known collisions, without establishing that remaining negatives are truly irrelevant.

[Krichene and Rendle (KDD 2020)](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) study evaluation sampling, not training objectives: sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model orderings even in expectation. Thus HR@10 against 99 negatives supports conclusions about that pinned protocol, not automatic claims about full-catalog HR@10 or which training loss is intrinsically superior.
